title: Prefix-KV stress pattern explorer: synthetic access mixes, burst priming, and memory pressure sweep
creator: Dylan Park
description: Create a repeatable, configurable harness that explores realistic stress patterns for the prefix-KV cache with the goal of mapping hit-rate vs p95 latency vs memory under mixed workloads. This ticket focuses on building the 'pattern explorer' orchestration, integrating production-derived sampling distributions (Zipf alpha, temporal locality windows, and prefix similarity histograms), and running an automated sweep that emits regression signals to the CI dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can generate three canonical access mixes (steady-state long-tail, microburst-dominant, and prefix-correlated sequences) using parameter files. 2) For each mix the harness reports tokens/sec, p95 latency, median latency, hit rate, memory RSS and cache occupancy at 1m intervals and stores artifacts to GCS. 3) Baseline run (run-id PR-BASE-20250218) captured and results validated against previous ENG baselines. 4) Regression detection rule emits an alert if p95 increases by >15% at same hit-rate bin or if hit-rate drops >5% for same memory budget. 5) All outputs appear on the runtime-kv-performance dashboard and a PR with run artifacts is opened.
test_plan: 1) Implement pattern generator modules: zipf_mixture, time_window_replay, prefix_similarity_sampler. 2) Wire generator to existing kv-sim harness (dockerized) with options for priming length, burst size, and concurrency. 3) Add instrumentation hooks: per-request timestamp, token_count, cache_lookup_result, KV-eviction events. 4) Define sweep matrix: memory budget [2G,4G,8G,16G], concurrency [8,32,128], burst_rate [no_burst, 100rps burst every 60s, continuous microburst]. 5) Run 3 warmup runs to prefill hotset and 5 measurement runs per cell. 6) Store raw traces and aggregated CSV to gs://redwood-kv-bench/pattern-explorer/{run-id}/. 7) Validate by comparing baseline run metrics and ensure regression detector thresholds fire as expected in synthetic regression injection test.
run_results: Baseline PR-BASE-20250218 completed: steady-state mix @8G mem, concurrency 32 -> tokens/sec 12480, p95 48ms, median 12ms, hit-rate 78.3%, RSS 7.6G. Microburst mix (same config) -> tokens/sec (avg) 13400, p95 210ms, median 18ms, hit-rate 74.1%, RSS 7.9G. Burst-primed with cold-start (no prefill) -> p95 1.1s and hit-rate 22%. Observed that increasing memory from 8G->16G improved hit-rate +6.5% but only reduced p95 by 12% for microburst workloads, indicating latency dominated by contention/eviction churn not just miss ratio. Artifacts: gs://redwood-kv-bench/pattern-explorer/PR-BASE-20250218/{metrics.csv,trace.jsonl,plots.tar.gz}.
notes_and_decisions: Opted to build the pattern generator as config-driven Python module instead of C++ extension to iterate faster and enable reuse by SRE for chaos tests.
We will keep default eviction policy LRU-approx; a follow-up ticket will sweep alternate policies (LIRS, ARC).
Regression detection: chosen simple delta-based threshold first (p95 >15% at same hit-rate bin), later replace with statistical two-sample test if false positives observed.
Memory accounting measured via container RSS + internal cache metadata; acknowledged +/-5% measurement noise — we'll average across runs.
Decided to record raw per-request latencies rather than only aggregates to enable p99 analysis later if needed.

review_feedback: Design review (2025-02-21): keep harness output schema stable (run-id, seed, config, aggregated metrics) so dashboard ingests reliably. Security review: no secrets in traces; PII scrubbed by prefix-scrubber module. Engineering review: prefer storing traces in compressed JSONL and derived CSVs for quick queries.
